name: Android
intro: The Compose SDK embeds the FarmerChat journey in a modern Android app. It is the reference flavour — the screens here are direct ports of the FarmerChat app itself, so this is the closest match to what farmers already use.
Everything ships as two artifacts: farmerchat-core (networking, session, state machines, no UI) and farmerchat-android-compose (the screens). You depend on the latter; it pulls in the former.

paras: The SDK artifacts are not published to a public repository yet. There is no Maven Central / GitHub Packages release, no CocoaPods trunk entry, and no npm package (npm view returns 404 for both JavaScript packages). The install steps below are the shape your integration will take, and they work today against a local build.
Until a release exists, build the SDK from source and consume it locally — each platform's install section shows the local path alongside the eventual remote one.

The SDK resolves from your declared repositories. Today that means your local Maven cache; a hosted repository slots into the same block when one exists.

tabs.label: Kotlin

blocks.html: Every surface of the journey can be switched off. The defaults give the full farmer experience; trim it to fit your app.

head: Option
What it controls
rows: Key for anonymous (guest) sessions. Required unless you supply your own token.
Google Geolocation key. Effectively required — the advice feed stays empty until a country resolves.
Initial language, e.g. "en", "hi". The farmer can change it in-journey.
Seed geography used before the farmer shares a location.
Trim the journey surface by surface.
Turn individual question modes and features off.
Opt into streaming agentic chat. Default off keeps the synchronous 1.0.0 contract.
Telemetry master switch. Default off — events are built but dropped until you opt in.
Supply your own identity instead of the SDK-owned phone/OTP flow.
Replace any server label. Keys must be canonical fc_v2_app_label_* keys.

blocks.html: Chat only
The most common trim: skip onboarding and the advice feed, and land the farmer directly in chat with history and language still reachable.

tabs.label: Kotlin
tabs.code:
FarmerChatConfig.Builder(FarmerChatEnvironment.PROD)
    .guestApiKey("<your guest API key>")
    .mode(FarmerChatMode.CHAT_ONLY)
    .showDrawer(false)    // moves history + language into the chat app bar
    .showHistory(true)    // past-advice icon
    .showSettings(false)
    .showNameScreen(false)
    .build()

paras: In CHAT_ONLY, showDrawer(false) is what moves history and language into the chat app bar — the drawer normally owns them. Setting showHistory(true) alone does nothing while the drawer is on.

blocks.html: Turn off a question mode

tabs.label: Kotlin
tabs.code:
FarmerChatConfig.Builder(FarmerChatEnvironment.PROD)
    .enableVoice(false)   // no mic on the composer or the home tiles
    .enableImages(false)  // no camera
    .build()

blocks.html: By default the SDK owns identity: farmers start as guests and can sign in with a phone number and OTP inside the journey. If your app already knows who the farmer is, supply the token instead and the SDK skips its own auth UI.

blocks.html: The SDK ships the FarmerChat look by default. Override the parts that must match your app — anything you leave unset keeps the FarmerChat value.

tabs.label: Kotlin
tabs.code:
FarmerChatConfig.Builder(FarmerChatEnvironment.PROD)
    .theme(
        FarmerChatTheme(
            brandPrimary = 0xFF00C950.toInt(),
            cardCornerRadius = 24,
            buttonCornerRadius = 999,  // fully rounded, the current default
            inputCornerRadius = 12
        )
    )
    .messageFontSizeSp(15f)
    .bubbleCornerRadius(18)
    .build()

paras: buttonCornerRadius defaults to 999 (a full pill) as of the 2026-09-15 design pass. Pass a smaller value to square them off.

blocks.html: All farmer-facing text is served by the backend and resolved per language, so the journey localises itself once the farmer picks a language. To override a specific string, key it by the canonical label key.

tabs.label: Kotlin
tabs.code:
FarmerChatConfig.Builder(FarmerChatEnvironment.PROD)
    .stringOverrides(
        mapOf(
            Labels.RECENT_CHATS to "Past advice",
            Labels.SHARE_LOCATION to "Share my farm"
        )
    )
    .build()

paras: Labels resolve as <key>_<lang> against the canonical fc_v2_app_label_* keys. A hand-typed short key silently never matches, and your override is ignored without an error. Always use the generated constants.

blocks.html: The SDK emits the same events the FarmerChat app tracks, with the same names and properties, through a listener you provide. It bundles no third-party analytics SDK — forward the events to whatever you already use.

tabs.label: Kotlin

paras: enableAnalytics defaults to false on every platform. Events are still constructed with their real names, properties and ordering — they are dropped at the single dispatch point, so enabling telemetry later cannot change any other behaviour.

blocks.html: The SDK requests permissions at the moment a farmer uses the feature, and degrades gracefully when one is refused. You declare them; the host app owns the manifest.

tabs.label: AndroidManifest.xml
tabs.code:
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE" />

<!-- Voice questions -->
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO" />
<!-- Photo questions -->
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" />
<uses-feature android:name="android.hardware.camera" android:required="false" />
<!-- Weather + location-specific advice -->
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION" />
<uses-feature android:name="android.hardware.location.gps" android:required="false" />

blocks.html: Only declare what you enable. If you set enableVoice(false), drop RECORD_AUDIO — a permission you never exercise still shows on your store listing.

name: iOS
intro: The SwiftUI SDK embeds the FarmerChat journey as a single view you can present or push. It targets iOS 16+ and ships as two Swift packages: FarmerChatCore (no UI) and FarmerChatSwiftUI (the screens).
If your app is UIKit-based, use the UIKit flavour instead — it targets iOS 15 and keeps SwiftUI out of its public surface.

Swift

let signedIn = FarmerChat.shared.isAuthenticated

)

)

blocks.html: The SDK emits the same events the FarmerChat app tracks, through a handler you provide. No third-party analytics SDK is bundled.

tabs.label: Swift
tabs.code:
FarmerChatConfig(
    environment: .prod,
    enableAnalytics: true, // default false
    onEvent: { name, props in MyAnalytics.track(name, props) },
    onChatOpened: { /* … */ },
    onMessageSent: { text in /* … */ },
    onAnswerReceived: { messageId in /* … */ },
    onScreenView: { screen in MyAnalytics.screen(screen) },
    onError: { code, message in MyLogger.warn(code, message) }
)

paras: enableAnalytics defaults to false on every platform. Events are still constructed with their real names, properties and ordering — they are dropped at the single dispatch point, so enabling telemetry later cannot change any other behaviour.

name: React Native
intro: The React Native SDK renders the journey with native components on both platforms from one JavaScript integration. It is a TypeScript package with peer dependencies on React Navigation, AsyncStorage and Expo AV.
Use it when you want a single integration across both stores. For deeper native control, the Android and iOS SDKs expose the same configuration surface.

paras: The SDK artifacts are not published to a public repository yet. There is no Maven Central / GitHub Packages release, no CocoaPods trunk entry, and no npm package (npm view returns 404 for both JavaScript packages). The install steps below are the shape your integration will take, and they work today against a local build.
Until a release exists, build the SDK from source and consume it locally — each platform's install section shows the local path alongside the eventual remote one.
